findings.finding: The chapter presents tableaux and names the prfTab tag, but the associated editorial sentence mistakenly calls the relevant proof system natural deduction.
findings.controlling_evidence: The directory, chapter identifiers, title, tag name and all fourteen imports identify the proof system as tableaux.
findings.required_translation_handling: Name tableaux and add an adjacent OLTETAB-001 note.

findings.finding: One problem writes A-or-B comma not-B inside the formula argument of one true-signed formula, although the tableau task requires three separate assumptions.
findings.controlling_evidence: The chapter defines a signed formula as exactly one sign/formula pair; A-or-B and not-B are distinct formulas, and false A is already separately signed.
findings.required_translation_handling: Split the two true assumptions, retain false A and add an adjacent OLTETAB-002 note.

findings.finding: The prose says lines 1 and 3 must be reused to close the branches, but line 3 is the checked negation and the needed false existential is line 4.
findings.controlling_evidence: The immediately preceding and following tableaux number the reusable true universal as 1 and false existential as 4; their rule labels are exactly the two named by the prose.
findings.required_translation_handling: Refer to lines 1 and 4 and add an adjacent OLTETAB-003 note.

findings.finding: The transitivity proof says individual formulas D_1 through D_m are a subset of Gamma rather than placing them in a finite set.
findings.controlling_evidence: The derivability definition quantifies over a finite subset, and the next display uses D_1 through D_m as a finite set of assumptions.
findings.required_translation_handling: Add set braces around the D-list and an adjacent OLTETAB-004 note.

findings.finding: Gamma_1 is defined as C_1 through C_n but the very next display uses C_1 through C_m.
findings.controlling_evidence: Gamma_0 and Gamma_1 are independent finite witnesses; the display and remainder of the proof consistently use m for the second witness.
findings.required_translation_handling: Use C_m in the definition and add an adjacent OLTETAB-005 note.

findings.finding: The transformation says true-negation is applied to false A rather than true not-A, labels the inserted false A as line n+1 although n+1 assumptions precede it, and contains a stray backslash before the display.
findings.controlling_evidence: The defined true-negation rule maps true not-A to false A; after replacing the first assumption, all n+1 assumptions remain before the inserted result, so the fixed line reference is not n+1.
findings.required_translation_handling: Name the correct rule input, refer generically to the newly inserted line, remove the stray character and add an adjacent OLTETAB-006 note.

findings.finding: Eight nodes use sFmla with the formula nested inside the sign argument, omitting the macro's required second argument.
findings.controlling_evidence: Every other node and the signed-formula definition use sFmla{Sign}{Formula}; the intended signs, formulas and branch closures are unambiguous from the rule applications.
findings.required_translation_handling: Restore all eight two-argument calls and add one adjacent OLTETAB-007 note.

findings.finding: The true- and false-universal cases state rule inputs with B(x), then state the conclusions and the semantic argument with A(x).
findings.controlling_evidence: Each tableau rule operates on one metavariable formula; all conclusions, substitution facts and the remainder of each case consistently use A.
findings.required_translation_handling: Use A throughout both universal cases and add an adjacent OLTETAB-008 note.

findings.finding: The explanation calls line 3 an instance of true A(s_2), though the shown line is eq(s_1,s_1) and the stated A(x)=eq(x,s_1) makes it A(s_1).
findings.controlling_evidence: The displayed tableau and the immediately following substitution calculation both identify A(s_1) as eq(s_1,s_1) and A(s_2) as the conclusion eq(s_2,s_1).
findings.required_translation_handling: Use A(s_1) for line 3 and add an adjacent OLTETAB-009 note.

findings.finding: The transitivity explanation says A(s_2) becomes eq(t_1,t_2), identified as line 2, but the stated t_1=s_2 and t_2=s_3 make that generic equality line 3.
findings.controlling_evidence: With A(x)=eq(s_1,x), A(s_2) is exactly eq(s_1,s_2), the formula visibly on line 2.
findings.required_translation_handling: Name eq(s_1,s_2) as line 2 and add an adjacent OLTETAB-010 note.

findings.finding: The case for the true equality rule says it adds signed A(t_2) with generic sign S, despite using true equality and true A(t_1) premises throughout.
findings.controlling_evidence: The displayed true equality rule concludes true A(t_2); the paragraph explicitly leaves the false equality rule to an analogous separate case.
findings.required_translation_handling: Use the true sign and add an adjacent OLTETAB-011 note.

findings.finding: The prose math span listing the two assumptions for the second tableau ends with an extra comma before the sentence continues.
findings.controlling_evidence: The displayed tableau has exactly the two listed assumptions and no third item; the analogous first case has no dangling list separator.
findings.required_translation_handling: Remove only the dangling comma and add an adjacent OLTETAB-012 note.
